proof.title: The first ghost lied
proof.lead: Each way of taking the wind out, against plain physics: points of the ride's time, mean of 10 rides
rows: All of it set to zero: the first ghost
Headwind turned around: the ghost now
proof.note: With no wind at all, TabPFN answered for a calm day inland: the wind had told it what kind of day it was.

lines: Wind: Open-Meteo · Météo-France AROME · ECMWF IFS

scenes.say: After a slow ride, the wind is the easy excuse. Was it really the wind?
wasitthewind is a small web app I host myself. Every ride I drop stays in the list.
After a ride, I drop the FIT file from my bike computer, and pick an earlier ride on the same loop.
The blue dot is my ghost: me on the same road, at the same power, with the wind taken out. TabPFN learned my legs from my other rides.
Thirty-five seconds in three hours. Another weather model and plain physics agree: it wasn't the wind.
Against the thirteenth of September on the same loop: sixteen minutes faster, and the wind cost me more, not less.
It counted once: a long one-way day in the north, with the wind at my back.
It gave me three and a half minutes, somewhere between one and six.
My first ghost lied. With the wind set to zero, TabPFN answered for a calm day inland. Turning the headwind around fixed it.
Open weights and open weather data, on my own machine.
